content.comment_body: Hello, I have configured a yearly timer and set the On and Off times using VM Parameters. I've created a web page that displays the timer outputs, allowing modifications to the timer directly from the web interface. However, I'm confused about interpreting the VM values. For example: setting the On Time to January 1st gives a VM value of 257, January 2nd results in 258, February 1st gives 513, and December 31st gives 4657. How can I determine the month and day from a single value? Please refer to the attached file for clarification.
The parameters for yearly or weekly timers use BCD coding. To view the analog values correctly, you need to select the block format as HEX. If you require an example, I can provide one.

Hello [user_name], Could you please share an example? I used the lighting section from the swimming pool sample included with [product_name] Web Editor and am attempting to add a monthly function to the timers. I can share my code if it helps.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are having difficulty understanding how timer parameters, shown in BCD-coded format, represent dates within yearly timers. The way VM parameters are presented is unintuitive, particularly when integrating with web interfaces, and lacks clear documentation or interface cues. Users are seeking better guidance or tools to connect coded timer values with readable dates.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect timer parameter values to be presented in a clear, straightforward format or to be well-documented, making conversion between coded values and calendar dates simple. They also hope for practical documentation or examples, especially when extending timer features.
